content_units: Best Checking Fit for a $1,200 Student Balance
For your priorities,   Account B is the best overall choice   because it has   no monthly fee   and no balance requirement.
With a typical student balance of   $1,200   and   2 ATM uses per month  , it avoids the biggest risk: recurring account fees.
Checking Account Comparison
Account   Monthly Fee   Fee Waiver   APY   ATM Benefit   Likely Cost for You
A   $12   Waived with direct deposit   0.01%   No ATM reimbursement     $0 if you have qualifying direct deposit; otherwise $12/mo
B   $0   None needed   0%   $3 per out-of-network ATM use     $0-$6/mo   depending on ATM choice
C   $5   Waived with $1,500 minimum balance   1.2%   Reimburses up to $10/mo in ATM fees     $5/mo fee likely applies
Student-Focused Recommendation
Option 1:   Account B     Best fee-avoidance pick for a student with  $1,200     No monthly fee
- Most predictable low-cost option.
- Even with   2 out-of-network ATM withdrawals  , your likely cost is about   $6/month  , and it could be   $0   if you use in-network ATMs.
- No need to maintain a higher balance or rely on direct deposit rules.
Option 2:   Account A     Good only if you reliably get qualifying direct deposit     Potentially free, but risky otherwise
- If your direct deposit qualifies every month, this could cost   $0  .
- But if it does not, the   $12 monthly fee   is worse than Account B’s ATM costs.
- The   0.01% APY   is effectively negligible on $1,200.
Option 3:   Account C     Best interest rate, but not best for your balance level     $1,500 needed to waive fee
- At   $1,200  , you likely pay the   $5 monthly fee  .
- The   1.2% APY   on $1,200 earns about   $14.40/year   before taxes, which is only about   $1.20/month  .
- That interest does   not   offset the monthly fee enough to beat Account B for fee avoidance.
Why Account B Wins for Your Situation
- Your balance is   below Account C’s $1,500 waiver threshold  .
- Your main goal is to   avoid fees  , not maximize interest.
- Two ATM uses per month is modest, so   Account B stays cheap  , especially if you can use your bank’s ATM network at least some of the time.
Quick Actions
- Re-check whether your income qualifies as   direct deposit   for Account A before considering it.
- If choosing   Account B  , look up the bank’s   ATM network   first to reduce or eliminate the $3 ATM charges.
Sources
- None needed; comparison based entirely on the account data you provided.
